title.narrative: Number of Business Service Centers (Vyapara Piyasa) established and offering financial, technical and ICT services and managed as viable business entities

description.narrative: Business Service Center is a onestop centre, which provides the services including government and financial services required for SMEs to improve their businesses on industry standards, maintain regulatory requirements and access to larger markets. Business Service Center provides services on marketing promotion, business ideas and business expansion, business registration, market facilitation, business consultation, Research and Development, Business Advisory Services, legal support services, technical advisory services and it creates linkages, procures goods and services for SMEs. The customer Segment of the Business Service centre is comprised of local SMEs, Business communities, Value Chain Actors and Youth and Women, who are not employed and expecting to start a business.

title.narrative: Percentage of projectsupported businesses run by both women and men demonstrating business growth in line with their business plans

description.narrative: Business Growth is defined as increase in Net Profit. Net profit is calculated by deducting the operational expenditures, loan interests and income tax from the sales revenues of the enterprise. Projectsupported enterprises increased their net profit by 1% or more in the current year compared with the baseline value of net profit of the enterprise prior to grant investment is considered as businesses demonstrating growth.

comment.narrative: According the final evaluation conducted by the external evaluators and Chrysaliss own data collection and internal database the project arrived at this percentage towards the end of the project.

title.narrative: The percentage of Praja Mandala and CDF members directly benefited through developmentoriented rural infrastructure

description.narrative: Praja Mandala is a legal entity under the Pradeshiya Sabha Act No. 15 of 1987 and registered under the office of Assistance Commissioner of Local Government. Community Development Forums (CDFs) are CBOs established in plantation sector to improve relationships between estate workers and management to advocate for resolving issues. The indicator measures direct beneficiaries of rural infrastructure development projects such as local farmers, small business owners, collectors, vendors, suppliers, and traders, who directly benefit from the infrastructures.

title.narrative: % of women and youthled MSMEs that have overcome the social norms which hinder women and youths ability to lead and run businesses

description.narrative: The indicator measures the percentage of women and youth led MSMEs demonstrated positive changes in gender norms related to access to finance, collateral assets, access to raw materials, safety, decision making and networking due to project interventions compared with the situation prior to project. The indicator tool consists of 27 norm statements. Social Norms are Standards and expectations to which women and men generally conform, within a range that defines a society, culture, and community at that point in time. Gender norms are ideas about how women and men should be and act. Internalized early in life, gender norms can establish a life cycle of gender socialization and stereotype.

title.narrative: Increased number of direct employment opportunities for youth and women in targeted areas

description.narrative: Direct attributable jobs created by the project supported enterprises for women and youth after the project interventions. Direct attributable jobs should represent the following two characteristics. The full time and parttime employees, contract producers, outgrowers, sales agents (who are directly involved in marketing SMEs products), who earn a minimum of LKR 10,000 of monthly income by the enterprise. The raw materials suppliers, crop farmers, collectors, earn an annual income of LKR 100,000 or more from the enterprise.
